## Functional acceptance

- [x] Plot window size now presents one representative value for uneven partitions.
      The regression fixture that formerly produced `32,540–32,541 bp per cell` now
      reports `≈32,541 bp per cell`; exact divisions and terminal `1 bp per cell`
      output remain unchanged.
- [x] For selected order A, B, C, X runs left to right as A, B, C while Y runs bottom
      to top in that same order. The three self plots occupy bottom-left, center, and
      top-right.
- [x] Every grid cell retains the contract “column is X, row is Y.” Opening the
      upper-left A-by-C cell selects X=A/Y=C, while its lower-right reciprocal selects
      X=C/Y=A.
- [x] A non-square, offset renderer fixture verifies the reciprocal canvas pixel by
      pixel as the exact transpose of its computed pair, including edge placement and
      bottom-up matrix coordinates.
- [x] Dragging a reorder handle on either X or Y changes one shared order on both axes.
      Keyboard arrow reordering preserves focus, self plots remain on the rising
      diagonal, and DOM traversal follows the visible top-to-bottom rows.
- [x] Reordering preserves the existing canvas nodes and image bytes and produces no
      additional worker preparation request. A moved reciprocal cell still opens with
      its displayed X/Y identities, and **Back to grid** restores the retained cell
      and focus.
- [x] Visual inspection of the browser capture confirmed that the drag grips remain
      adjacent to their sequence names and the reordered row labels stay aligned with
      the plot matrix.

## Local toolchain note

On the macOS validation host, the pinned Rust 1.98.0 toolchain was installed without a
`rustc` proxy in the child shell and its `rust-lld` runtime path was not discoverable
automatically. The pinned binary paths and a temporary linker wrapper supplied that
runtime path. Restricted `wasm-pack` execution also required one approved download of
its pinned `wasm-bindgen` helper. The complete release build then passed; these were
local toolchain-environment constraints rather than source failures.
